neet_phy_u17_t00_1.working: Photon energy is E = hν, which depends only on frequency. Doubling intensity doubles the number of photons, not the energy of each photon.

neet_phy_u17_t00_2.working: E = 1240/620 = 2 eV = 3.2e-19 J. N = 6.4/3.2e-19 = 2e19 photons per second.

neet_phy_u17_t00_4.working: Photons carry no charge, so a magnetic field exerts no force on them and they are not deflected. A is false; R is true.

neet_phy_u17_t00_5.working: N = Pλ/(hc), so for equal power a longer wavelength gives more photons per second: I is correct. p = hν/c, so doubling ν doubles p: II is correct.
